chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Safwan from al-'Is ibn al-Qasim said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the woman with continuous menstruation (al-mustahadha) who enters into ihram, and he mentioned Asma bint Umays, saying: 'Indeed, Asma bint Umys gave birth to her son Muhammad at al-Baida', and her childbirth was a blessing for the women; whoever gave birth from them or had menstruation, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) commanded her to perform istifrad (rinsing the womb), gird herself with a belt, and enter into ihram.'

And whenever she forgot the ihram or was ignorant of it until the time passed, if there is a miqat upon her, let her return to the miqat of her people; if there is no miqat upon her, let her enter into ihram from the place where she arrived. And if she had already entered the Haram (sanctuary), let her go out to the outside of the Haram if she is able to do so; and if she is not able to do so, let her enter into ihram from her place, and there is no penalty upon her.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a woman with continuous menstruation entering ihram for Hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the precedent of Asma bint Umays, a prominent companion, to justify the ruling for women with istihadha (continuous bleeding) who can enter ihram after ritual cleansing and binding the flow. It provides a detailed jurisprudential framework for rectifying missed or forgotten ihram obligations, distinguishing between those with a designated miqat and those without, and offering practical solutions for those already within the Haram boundaries. This ruling underscores the flexibility in Shia fiqh for accommodating physiological conditions without invalidating the pilgrimage.
